# Paññāparihīna Sutta (Iti 41 (It 2.14 PTS It 35))

**ID:** Iti 41 (It 2.14 PTS It 35)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Paññāparihīna Sutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Bereft of Wisdom
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/iti41
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paññāparihīna Sutta* ("Bereft of Wisdom", Iti 41 / It 2.14, PTS It 35) is a discourse found in the second chapter (*Dukanipāta*) of the *Itivuttaka* that addresses the value and rewards of noble discernment [SuttaCentral]. Secondary discussion of the sutta quotes its core verse praising wisdom as supreme in the world (*paññā hi seṭṭhā lokasmiṁ*) because it leads to penetration or breakthrough (*nibbedhagāminī*) and properly makes known the exhaustion of birth and continued existence (*jātibhavaparikkhayaṁ*), linking it to the overcoming of defilements and mistaken views [War Yar Mein Da 2015].

Passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral include the *Mārgavarga* of various *Udānavarga* traditions—such as the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 12, UVS 12), the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 12), and Chinese translations including T 210.28, T 212.13, and T 213.12 [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also identifies a resembling parallel in the *Dvayatānupassanā Sutta* (Snp 3.12) and notes citations of the discourse in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37) and *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2 and Pe 3) [SuttaCentral]. Cross-language machine alignments from DharmaNexus confirm this connection, matching verses in Iti 41 (§3.1–3.3) with the Sanskrit *Udānavarga de Subaši* (§418) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus identifies shared passages across eleven texts, with the most extensive text reuse occurring in the *Tikanipāta* (AN 3), *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5), *Chakkanipāta* (AN 6), *Lakkhaṇa Sutta* (DN 30), the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37), and adjacent suttas of the *Itivuttaka* (Iti 28, Iti 29, Iti 46) [DharmaNexus].
